matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and verify they are equal; without this, a syntactically correct equation may still be numerically false.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a stick move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a change that leaves the equation "XVII = XVII - XVIII" without noticing that 17 ≠ -1.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a valid Roman numeral; without this, the solver may create symbols like a lone diagonal line that are not Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick move that affects a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical stick from an "I" and leaving no character.

matchstick.title: Operator stick composition
matchstick.principle: Know the exact stick count and orientation for each allowed operator (+, -, =); without this, the solver may produce invalid operators such as a plus sign missing its vertical stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick to or from an operator.
matchstick.example: Adding a diagonal stick to "-" and assuming it becomes "+".

matchstick.title: Allowed operators only
matchstick.principle: The final equation may contain only '+', '-', and '=', and you must not introduce any other symbol; without this, the solver may create a non‑allowed operator like "×" or a malformed "=".
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move that changes an operator.
matchstick.example: Turning "-" into a "≠" sign by adding a diagonal.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you cannot replace a vertical stick with a diagonal or horizontal one; without this, the solver may reshape symbols incorrectly.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick onto a horizontal "-" and treating the result as "+".

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect only the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick); without this, the solver may inadvertently add or delete sticks.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from "=" and not adding it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one "=" sign, which must remain the standard two‑horizontal‑stick form; without this, the solver may break the equality sign or create multiple "=" signs.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering any stick move involving the "=" sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from "=" and turning it into a "-" sign.

matchstick.title: Operator source/destination validity
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from an operator, the source must remain a valid operator (+, -, =); when adding a stick to an operator, the result must be a valid operator and respect orientation; without this, the solver may leave "-" empty or create an undefined operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick move that touches an operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the only stick from "-" and leaving no operator, or adding a diagonal to "-" and assuming it becomes "+".

matchstick.title: Transform X↔V while preserving numeral validity
matchstick.principle: When converting between X and V, move a diagonal stick appropriately so both characters stay valid (X needs two crossing diagonals, V needs two meeting diagonals); without this, a naive removal creates an invalid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick move involves X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and expecting the remainder to be a valid V, ignoring the required meeting‑at‑bottom geometry.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: Provide the corrected equation as a single line prefixed with "Correct version of the equation: ", using uppercase and collapsed whitespace; without this, the answer is not recognized by the scorer.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the end of the solution, before output.
matchstick.example: Outputting just "XVII - XVII" instead of the required prefixed line.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual changes and forgets to check whether the numeric equality actually holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the values of both sides after a proposed move and confirm they match.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks without ensuring the remaining or resulting glyph matches a Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that both source and destination characters are valid Roman numerals after the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model adds or removes sticks from operators without respecting their defined stick patterns.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Refer to the operator stick composition table before modifying an operator.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effectively removing a stick)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it onto another, violating the one‑stick‑move rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure every stick taken from a source character is added to a destination character.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from an operator leaving it non‑existent or adds a stick of wrong orientation, producing an undefined operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the "Operator source/destination validity" skill: verify both source and destination operators remain valid after the move.
